svg.text: Phase 7W/7X: Why 150Â° & 165Â° work but 30Â° & 45Â° fail with J5-only
1) Successful J5-only cases
Yaw 150Â° â success, J5 = -153.7Â°, lift â 52.0 mm
Yaw 165Â° â success, J5 = -138.7Â°, lift â 52.0 mm
J5 axis dot world-Z â 0.9995, so wrist-roll behaves almost like tabletop yaw.
Fixed jaw approaches near the bottle center without penetration.
2) Failed J5-only cases
Yaw 30Â° â nearest candidate fixed-gap = -1.80 mm (penetration)
Yaw 45Â° â nearest candidate fixed-gap = -4.61 mm (penetration)
Not a J5-range problem: the fixed jaw enters the bottle side before a valid central grasp is formed.
Likely cause: front/back relation of the fixed jaw becomes unfavorable.
3) Recovery idea (Phase 7X)
Keep J1-J4 fixed. Add only:
â¢ J5 yaw adaptation
â¢ small bottle XY offsets (Â±10 mm, step 2.5 mm)
Shift bottle center a few mm so the fixed jaw hits the center region instead of penetrating.
Interpretation
â¢ 150Â° / 165Â° success means the mechanism can tolerate some large yaw changes with J5 alone.
â¢ 30Â° / 45Â° failure does NOT mean "J5 is insufficient" in torque or range. The geometry fails first.
â¢ The main suspect is the fixed jaw's front/back relation to the bottle. Reversing J5 is not enough if the jaw reaches the wrong side.
â¢ Therefore the next efficient test is small XY correction + J5, rather than redoing all of J1-J4 or changing the whole simulator.
â¢ Failure videos are useful because they reveal whether the miss is penetration, side-push, or losing bilateral contact during J6 closure.
Recommended next action:
Run Phase 7X for yaw 30Â° and 45Â° with J5 + XY recovery, while also saving failure videos.
